category_title: Highly anxious or extremely shy students at risk of disengagement
minimal_context: The student is sitting in a small group cluster using drawing software to create a digital picture about fairness and honesty.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please open the drawing software tool and create a digital picture showing your ideas about fairness and honesty.

STUDENT: (Looks down at the desk, keeping her hands in her lap instead of touching the mouse) I... I don't know what to draw.

TUTOR: You can draw something about fair play or no cheating. Just give it a try.

STUDENT: (Stares at the blank screen on the drawing software, looking highly anxious) It's too hard to draw that on the computer. I don't know how.

TUTOR: Just do your best. The rest of your group is already working on their pictures.

STUDENT: (Pushes the mouse away and turns her chair away from the desk, refusing to look at the screen) I'm not doing it. I can't do it.

options.A: Frame students as 'professional digital artists'; justify mundane tasks (like saving files) by comparing them to professional design standards.
options.B: Develop the task into a drama project, with children collaboratively writing, planning, and acting out a play about fairness.
options.C: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing the digital picture using the drawing software tool during the session.
options.D: Seat students in such a way as to facilitate small group work, with communal stationery in each cluster of desks.
